item: Auth trust — no auto-link on a provider email, the second factor on SSO, link from settings, provider env_file

rulings: 1. Never auto-link on a provider-asserted email; a provider-created account is matched by subject only
2. The second factor applies to provider sign-ins (OIDC and ATProto)
3. Link from settings; the callback is session-aware and never switches accounts
4. Compose passthrough for the per-provider variables, plus a typed 503 when none are configured

not_lab_observed.statement: code-only slice: no Dex, no hostile-provider fixture, no browser, no containers. The proof is unit and integration tests plus CI.
not_lab_observed.rerun: the A05 OIDC lab (Dex 2.45.1 + the stdlib hostile provider under docs/evidence/)
rerun_must_prove: the takeover A05 measured is gone AGAINST DEX: a second configured provider asserting the owner's address email_verified redirects ?oauth_error=email_conflict and issues no session
the settings Connect control completes a real Dex round trip and the identity appears in /me/oauth-identities

a signed-in browser that starts an ordinary login flow as an UNLINKED Dex user lands ?link=dex, and as ANOTHER account's user lands ?link_error=identity_belongs_to_another_account, with the session still the one it started as
an MFA-enrolled account signing in through Dex lands ?mfa=required with the vidra_mfa_pending cookie set, and a real authenticator code at POST /auth/mfa/challenge issues the session
the mfa token appears in NO access log line, NO Referer header and NO history entry on the real proxy the lab runs
an operator flow: cp env/oauth.env.example env/oauth.env, fill it, and a containerised api boots with the provider complete (the render is proven here; the BOOT through env_file is not)
begin answers 503 oauth_not_configured with OAUTH_PROVIDERS unset against the real binary
not_lab_observed.still_unverified_unchanged: no hosted IdP (Google/Okta/Entra quirks: audience arrays, email_verified as a string, non-RS256 id_tokens); no https PUBLIC_BASE_URL; no provider-initiated or back-channel logout (vidra implements neither)

collision_matrix.rule: an account is matched by the issuer-scoped SUBJECT; an email match is a refusal

rows.attempt: existing PASSWORD account's address, email_verified true
rows.note: this is the row that used to link; the owner takeover rode in on it

rows.attempt: existing PASSWORD account's address, email_verified false
rows.note: byte-identical to the verified answer, so the response cannot be probed for whether the provider verified

rows.attempt: no local account with that address
rows.answer: account created, email_verified inherited from the claim

rows.attempt: PROVIDER-created account, re-login by the SAME subject
a DIFFERENT provider asserting the PROVIDER-created account's address, verified
rows.note: the subject rule; a provider-created account has no password to compare and an address the FIRST provider put there

tests: vidra-core internal/httpapi/oauth_test.go TestOAuthRefusesToClaimAnExistingAccountByEmail (httptest fake OIDC provider: real discovery + JWKS + RS256 id_tokens)
collision_matrix.audit: a refused collision emits auth.login failure oauth_email_conflict and NO auth.oauth.link success row (asserted)

mfa_on_sso.mechanism: one door: auth.Service.providerSession. Five call sites reached issueTokens directly (three in auth/oauth.go, two in auth/atproto.go) and none consulted mfaEnabled.
mfa_on_sso.withheld: the callback issues no session and mints the SAME single-purpose mfa_token auth.Service.Login mints; POST /auth/mfa/challenge is unchanged

transport.chosen: httpOnly cookie vidra_mfa_pending; the landing URL carries only the flag ?mfa=required
transport.rejected: a one-time ?mfa=<token> on the landing URL
transport.why: unlike the step-up assertion (?step_up=<token>), which is bound to the session it was minted for and authorises nothing without it, an mfa_token is bound to NO session — it IS the first factor, standing in for a password already proven. A query parameter would put it in the browser history, in the Referer of every same-origin subresource the landing page fetches, and in the access log of the frontend server and any reverse proxy. Three places a password would never be written.
transport.samesite_lax_because: the cookie must survive the top-level GET back from the identity provider
transport.ttl: 300s, equal to auth.mfaTokenTTL, so the browser stops sending a token the server would refuse rather than the two disagreeing about when the challenge died
transport.single_use: cleared the moment it authorises a session, and cleared when the token cannot be resolved at all (nothing left to spend). KEPT across a wrong code: a typo is not a use, and the password path lets you retype too.

mfa_on_sso.contract_change: MFAChallengeRequest.mfa_token becomes OPTIONAL (required: [code]); the body still wins when both are present, so the password path is unchanged and does not read the cookie
mfa_on_sso.recovery_codes: work on a provider challenge (asserted) — an account that lost its authenticator must not be locked out of its own sign-in method
mfa_on_sso.limiter: unchanged: the challenge stays behind the strict per-IP auth limiter
mfa_on_sso.frontend: the login page reads ?mfa=required and shows the challenge it already had; completeMfaChallenge takes string|null and OMITS the field for the cookie path (sending null would be a supplied-and-empty token, which is 422). The signup page redirects ?mfa=required to /login?mfa=required: an account that needs a code already exists.
tests: vidra-user e2e/oauth.spec.ts 'a provider sign-in with two-factor lands on the challenge and finishes without a token' (asserts the request body has NO mfa_token)

start_oidc.seals: purpose:"link" + uid + sid inside the SIGNED vidra_oauth_state cookie (the core #217 step-up pattern)
start_oidc.response: {authorization_url} as JSON, not a 302 — the request must carry the caller's bearer token, which a top-level navigation cannot send
start_oidc.401: anonymous, or a request not bound to a session
start_oidc.404: unknown provider name on an instance that HAS providers
start_oidc.422: provider_already_linked — this account already holds an identity for this provider, refused BEFORE the round trip (no state cookie is sealed)
start_oidc.503: oauth_not_configured — the instance has no providers at all

start_atproto.extra: 409 identity_belongs_to_another_account is answered HERE, not at the callback, because ATProto resolves its subject (the DID) at Begin — before the browser leaves. OIDC cannot know its subject until the id_token comes back, so that one is a redirect code.

callback_link.success: 302 to return_to with ?link=<provider>; no session is minted and no refresh cookie set — the caller already has the session the link belongs to
callback_link.failures: ?link_error=<code> for an attempt started at /link/start; ?oauth_error=<code> for a LOGIN-purpose callback that turned into a link because a session was already in the browser — the failure key follows the ORIGIN page, because a refusal the landing page does not render is a silent one. Codes either way: identity_belongs_to_another_account, provider_already_linked, account_disabled, link_failed, oauth_exchange_failed, atproto_upstream, atproto_identity_mismatch
callback_link.vocabulary: deliberately separate from oauth_error: a link is not a sign-in, and the page receiving it is the settings page (the same reasoning step-up applies to step_up_error)
callback_link.idempotent: re-linking the SAME subject to the SAME account is not an error — a second click on Connect is not a mistake

login_callback_inside_a_session.rule: a login-purpose callback arriving with a LIVE refresh session is a link attempt for that session, or a refusal — never an account switch
login_callback_inside_a_session.measured_before: A05 watched a signed-in browser go from `newcomer` to a freshly created `mfauser`
login_callback_inside_a_session.session_read: auth.Service.SessionAccount reads the refresh cookie WITHOUT rotating it — a callback that answered the question with Refresh would rotate the caller's token as a side effect of looking, and the bearer token cannot ride a top-level navigation from an IdP
login_callback_inside_a_session.refusal_visible: the refusal lands as ?oauth_error=identity_belongs_to_another_account, which the login page already renders; the copy names the door ('sign out first, then sign in with it') rather than only reporting the refusal

link_contract.email_verified: set locally when a provider-verified email is what authorised the link AND it is the account's OWN address (case-insensitive). A verified claim about a DIFFERENT address changes nothing. Best-effort — a failure here does not undo a completed link.
link_contract.unlink: unchanged: 422 with the set-a-password remedy on the last sign-in method, 404 for a provider that is not linked
link_contract.refusal_shapes: 409 identity_belongs_to_another_account and 422 provider_already_linked are typed errors rendered by the central handler wherever the answer is JSON; the SAME machine codes ride ?link_error= where the answer is a browser redirect

env_file.problem: vidra-core's compose environment map is an explicit allow-list, and it cannot name a key whose NAME is derived from the operator's provider list (OAUTH_PROVIDERS=okta -> OAUTH_OKTA_ISSUER/_CLIENT_ID/_CLIENT_SECRET/_SCOPES). A05 measured a filled env file delivering exactly ONE OAuth variable — OAUTH_PROVIDERS — after which the api refused to boot for the other three.
env_file.change: vidra-core/docker-compose.yml: api AND worker gain `env_file: [{path: ./env/oauth.env, required: false}]` (Compose >= 2.24 long syntax — the meta AGENTS.md rule 4 floor)
env_file.worker_too_because: a worker runs the same binary through the same config.Load; a provider complete for api and incomplete for worker is half a split deployment refusing to boot
env_file.precedence: `environment:` wins over `env_file:` in Compose, so nothing in the tracked compose file can be silently overridden by dropping a file beside it
env_file.values: read as literal KEY=VALUE, NOT compose substitution — a $ in a client secret needs no escaping

renders_measured.without_the_file: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file env/production.env.example --profile core --profile frontend --profile edge config -q → exit 0, render unchanged
renders_measured.delivery: with OAUTH_PROVIDERS=okta and a filled env/oauth.env, the rendered api AND worker environment each carry OAUTH_OKTA_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET, OAUTH_OKTA_ISSUER, OAUTH_OKTA_SCOPES and OAUTH_PROVIDERS — five keys where A05 measured one

validate_lane.assert: meta-ci 'Every config key vidra-core reads has a compose consumer'
validate_lane.treatment: NO CHANGE NEEDED, and this was checked rather than assumed. The assert extracts keys by regex from config.go — getEnv*/p.Str/p.Int/p.Int64/p.Bool/p.Duration followed by a LITERAL "[A-Z0-9_]+". The per-provider names are built by concatenation (prefix := "OAUTH_" + strings.ToUpper(...)), so the regex never sees them: the only OAUTH key it extracts is OAUTH_PROVIDERS, which has had a compose consumer all along.
validate_lane.run_locally: the exact CI step re-run in the meta worktree: OK: all 176 config keys reach BOTH api and worker (177 entries in each map)
validate_lane.api_worker_equality: still holds — env_file keys appear in both rendered maps or in neither

docs: vidra-core/docs/operations.md gains 'Single sign-on (OIDC) — the one family of settings compose cannot allow-list'

meta env/production.env.example and env/staging.env.example: the per-provider variables move OUT of the template and point at vidra-core/env/oauth.env.example; the UNPROVEN banner is replaced by the two trust rules
env_file.setup_engine: `vidra setup --template env/production.env.example` still writes no '# Managed by' block (re-run locally) — the engine collects no OAUTH answer, so removing the commented per-provider lines cannot strand one

typed_503.change: OAUTH_PROVIDERS unset makes GET /auth/oauth/{provider} and its callback answer 503 oauth_not_configured, matching ATProto's disabled path
typed_503.was: 404, which A05 recorded as coherent but the wrong shape — a client could not tell 'you named a provider this instance does not have' from 'this instance does not do SSO'
typed_503.unchanged: an unknown name on an instance that HAS providers is still 404

migration.why_none: oauth_identities already carries UNIQUE (provider, subject) and UNIQUE (user_id, provider) from migration 0055 — exactly the two refusals the link contract needs. Core stays at schema 144.

(59.1s), all ok, against a native Postgres 16.15 on 127.0.0.1:55491 initdb'd EMPTY and migrated 0 -> 144 in one run (dirty=false) plus a native Redis on :56491. -p 1 because those packages share one database.

user.vitest: 2639 of 2643 across 264 files; the 4 failures are the known suite-interaction flake on this machine — all four pass when run alone, and three (AdminTable, Modal, ResetPasswordForm) are files this slice does not touch
user.regen: lib/api/generated.ts regenerated from the core spec — contract-ci ordering is core, then user

recorded_not_fixed: a per-provider trusted_email_domains allow-list stays a later option: it would let an operator say 'this IdP may auto-link addresses at corp.example', which is a real convenience for a single-IdP instance and a second trust surface for a two-IdP one. Not needed to close the takeover, so not built.

the ATProto Connect control needs a handle before the handoff, so it expands an inline field rather than navigating on the first click — a small asymmetry with the OIDC rows that is inherent to the protocol
an identity for a provider the operator has switched OFF stays listed and unlinkable (asserted), because hiding it would make it invisible and unremovable
